accepted.question_text: Suppose f and g are distinct non-constant meromorphic functions that share four distinct values a1, a2, a3, and a4 in the sense that, for each shared value a_nu, the set of points where f = a_nu is the same as the set of points where g = a_nu, but no agreement of multiplicities is assumed. Must Nevanlinna's Four-Value conclusion still hold: after relabelling the shared values, must the cross-ratio (a1, a2, a3, a4) equal -1, so that a1 and a2 are Picard values of both functions and g is a Mobius transformation of f that fixes a3 and a4 and permutes a1 and a2?
accepted.context_brief: Nevanlinna four shared values without multiplicity agreement

evidence.quote: Four-Value-Theorem (Nevanlinna [13]). Let f and g be non-constant meromorphic functions sharing values aν (1 ≤ ν ≤ 4), but now specifically by counting multiplicities. Then (relabelling the values, if necessary) (a1, a2, a3, a4) = (f, g, a3, a4) = -1 holds. In particular, a1 and a2 are Picard values of f and g, and g is a Mobius transformation of f that fixes a3 and a4 and permutes a1 and a2.
In [4] G. Gundersen attributed the question, whether the Four-Value-Theorem also holds without the condition by counting multiplicities, to L. Rubel.
In the same paper, however, Gundersen also provided the first counterexample to Nevanlinna's conjecture and thus destroyed the hope for a (0+4)-Theorem.

accepted.question_text: Suppose f and g are non-constant meromorphic functions that share four distinct values, and one of those four shared values is shared by counting multiplicities, meaning that for that one value the two functions take the value at exactly the same points with the same multiplicities, while for the other three values only the sets of shared points are assumed to coincide. Must the conclusion of Nevanlinna's Four-Value Theorem still follow, namely that after relabelling the values the cross-ratio (a1, a2, a3, a4) equals -1, a1 and a2 are Picard values of both functions, and g is a Mobius transformation of f that fixes a3 and a4 and permutes a1 and a2?

accepted.question_text: Can the general problem of two meromorphic functions sharing four values be reduced by Zalcman rescaling to a limit pair with bounded spherical derivative without losing the essential shared-value data? More precisely, after passing to rescaled limits, can one rule out the possibilities that a value shared by the original pair becomes only a Picard value of the limit pair, that a value not originally shared by counting multiplicities becomes shared by counting multiplicities in the limit, or that the two limit functions collapse to the identical function, so that a proof of the (1+3) conjecture in the bounded-spherical-derivative setting would imply the general case?
accepted.context_brief: Open rescaling reduction for the (1+3) problem

evidence.quote: Under certain circumstances it may happen that a problem for meromorphic function of arbitrary order of growth can be reduced to a problem for functions of finite order by the well-known Zalcman Lemma [26]. This might also be the case here, although there are some obstacles, as will be seen later.

Till now, however, it cannot be excluded that (a) a shared value gets lost in the sense that it becomes a Picard value for f-hat and g-hat, although it is not for f and g; (b) multiplicities get lost in the sense that f-hat and g-hat share some value aν by counting multiplicities, although f and g do not; (c) f-hat = g-hat (worst case).

But even if f-hat ≠ g-hat holds and the (3+1)-Conjecture turns out to be true for functions with bounded spherical derivative, we can only deduce (a1, a2, a3, a4) = -1, except if we are able to rule out also the first and second case.
